# Gate Requirements Checklist: The template typechecks, and the gate runs it

**Purpose**: Validate the quality of the requirements for putting TypeScript into this repo's gate — completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability and coverage — before any code is written.
**Created**: 2026-11-11
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are requirements defined for each of the two distinct error classes the spec measures, TS2307 and TS2339? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-002] — FR-001 covers the TS2307 class, FR-002 the TS2339 class, each named with its cause.
- [x] CHK002 Is a requirement stated for where in the `verify` chain the new step runs, not only that it runs? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004] — FR-004 fixes the position (after `build:tokens`) and says the other steps keep their order.
- [x] CHK003 Are the documents that must be updated enumerated rather than referred to as "the docs"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005] — FR-005 omitted `docs/architecture.md`, which the plan and T015 both change; it now names it.
- [x] CHK004 Is a requirement stated for what must NOT be done to reach zero errors? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK005 Are requirements defined for files inside `tsconfig.json`'s `include` that the spec does not name — `tokens/scripts` and `.storybook` — or is their current state assumed clean? [Gap, Spec §FR-006] — closed: FR-006 was added for this, and it covers the whole program rather than listing directories.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is "an ambient declaration covers `*.module.css` imports" specific enough to be satisfied only one way, or could a reader satisfy it by widening `compilerOptions.types` instead? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001] — ambiguous at the spec level on purpose — FR-001 states the outcome; the plan picks the local declaration over `compilerOptions.types` and says why.
- [x] CHK007 Is "inside `tsconfig.json`'s program" defined, given that a file can be in `include` or reached by an import? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, §FR-002] — the plan distinguishes a file reached by `include` from one reached by an import, which is the whole cause of the 8 TS2339.
- [x] CHK008 Does the spec distinguish the `types/` directory it adds from `compilerOptions.types`, which is a different field with a similar name? [Ambiguity, Plan § Technical context] — the plan contrasts the `types/` directory with the `compilerOptions.types` field explicitly.
- [x] CHK009 Is the exact command the `typecheck` script must run specified, rather than left as "run TypeScript"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003] — FR-003 names `tsc --noEmit`, and the plan says why the flag is repeated when the config already sets it.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Do the spec's FR-007 and its success criterion on `@ts-ignore` state the same prohibition without one being broader than the other? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK011 Does the plan's chain position for `typecheck` match the spec's FR-004, and does tasks.md repeat the same position? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, Plan, Tasks §T007] — FR-004, the plan's chain paragraph and T007 all say after `build:tokens`, before `prettier:check`.
- [x] CHK012 Is the error count stated consistently as twelve across the spec, the plan and the issue body? [Consistency] — twelve, 4 + 8, in the spec's overview, the plan, the issue body and the runnable line's red note.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK013 Is exactly one success criterion marked as the runnable line, and does it fail on today's `develop`? [Measurability, Spec § Success criteria] — one `**Runnable:**` line, `npx tsc --noEmit`; run on the branch point this pass, exit 2, 12 errors.
- [x] CHK014 Is the criterion "`npm run verify` fails when a component is given a type error" objectively checkable, given that the error must be introduced on purpose and reverted? [Measurability, Spec § Success criteria] — T008 specifies introducing the error, the expected failure, the revert, and quoting it in the PR.
- [x] CHK015 Can "the docs say the gate typechecks" be objectively verified, or does it rest on a reviewer's reading? [Measurability, Spec § Success criteria] — as measurable as a docs criterion gets — T012 to T015 name the sentence to change in each file.
- [x] CHK016 Is the constraint that nothing was silenced expressed as something a reviewer can run, even though it is deliberately not the runnable line? [Measurability, Spec § Success criteria] — the criterion carries the grep and says why it is deliberately not the runnable line.

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK017 Are requirements defined for the primary flow — a contributor running the gate locally — and for the same gate running in CI? [Coverage, Spec § User scenarios] — scenario 2 names both `npm run verify` locally and `build / ci`.
- [x] CHK018 Are requirements defined for the copy-taker scenario, where someone has renamed the template and runs `tsc` in their own repo? [Coverage, Spec § User scenarios] — scenario 1 is the copy-taker opening a copy in an editor.
- [x] CHK019 Are requirements stated for running the type check on its own, separate from the full chain? [Coverage, Spec §FR-003] — scenario 3 and FR-003 both cover running the check on its own.

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK020 Does the spec say what happens if adding `vitest.setup.ts` to the program surfaces NEW errors that do not exist today? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-006] — closed: FR-006 now says any such error is fixed the same way and none is excluded, and T005 makes it a task.
- [x] CHK021 Are requirements defined for the files `include` still excludes, so that a future reader knows the exclusion is deliberate and not an oversight? [Coverage, Spec § Out of scope] — the out-of-scope section names `scripts/`, `.specify/` and `tokens/scripts/*.test.mjs` as deliberately outside the program.
- [x] CHK022 Is the behaviour specified for a `.module.css` import whose class names are read dynamically, which the declared record type permits but does not check? [Edge Case] — the record type admits any key by design; that is the standard CSS-modules declaration and no requirement is owed.

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK023 Is the cost of the added step stated, so that nobody has to re-derive whether a billed job or minute was added? [Completeness, Plan § Surfaces touched] — the plan's `cost` line: no job, no trigger, seconds inside an already-billed one.
- [x] CHK024 Are requirements stated for the required-check names, so a reader knows no branch ruleset edit is owed? [Coverage, Plan § Surfaces touched] — the plan's `build-check.yml` line says the check keeps its name, so no ruleset edit is owed.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK025 Is the assumption that `@chrisgriffin/config/tsconfig.json`'s strictness is the intended level stated rather than implied? [Assumption, Spec § Out of scope] — the out-of-scope section states that the inherited strictness level is what is being enforced, not raised.
- [x] CHK026 Is the assumption documented that `scripts/init.mjs` needs no change, and is it clear what would prove it wrong? [Assumption, Tasks §T017] — T017 states the assumption and names `init / ci` as what would disprove it.
- [x] CHK027 Is it stated that no new dependency is required, so a reviewer is not left to infer it? [Dependency, Gap, Plan § Technical context] — closed: the plan states it. Corrected in review: bringing `.storybook` into the program needed `@types/node`, so the plan now names that one dev dependency and what `package-lock.json` gains.

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK028 Does the spec's out-of-scope list resolve, rather than leave open, whether the unreferenced-token findings belong to this change? [Ambiguity, Spec § Out of scope] — **left open, deliberately.** The spec puts them out of scope, which settles this change; what it cannot settle is whether the 48 `tokens/token-unreferenced` findings should be trimmed or kept as a complete scale. That is the repo owner's call, not this ticket's, and it is reported rather than decided here. Open here because the question is genuinely unanswered, not because the spec is wrong.
- [x] CHK029 Is there any conflict between FR-007's ban on removing an `include` entry and FR-001/FR-002's requirement to add two? [Conflict] — resolved: no. FR-007 bans removing an entry to drop its errors; FR-001 and FR-002 add entries. Adding is not removing.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
